short: The first direct clash between Allied and German forces on land, resulting in the German occupation of Norway.
full:
On 9 April 1940, Germany launched a surprise invasion of Denmark and Norway to secure iron ore shipments from Sweden and establish naval bases on the Atlantic coast. British and French forces were dispatched to support the Norwegians, engaging in several naval battles and landing troops in central and northern Norway. Despite initial Allied naval successes, German air superiority and rapid ground advances proved decisive.

The Allied forces were eventually forced to evacuate in June 1940 as the situation in France deteriorated. The campaign secured Germany's northern flank and vital resources for the remainder of the war, but it also resulted in heavy losses for the German surface fleet. The political fallout in Britain led to the resignation of Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain, who was replaced by Winston Churchill.
